newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ minister says Iran withdrawing envoy.
newsitem.headline: NZ minister says Iran withdrawing envoy.

text.p: New Zealand's International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith said on Monday Iran was recalling its ambassador from Wellington in a diplomatic row over a German court ruling that Tehran ordered political killings.
"Their ambassador is...being recalled," he told a news conference, adding he expected the envoy's absence would be temporary. New Zealand recalled its ambassador to Tehran on Friday.
Iran's withdrawal is in line with moves on Sunday when it recalled envoys to all European Countries except Greece.

This in turn was sparked by international action led by Europe temporarily recalling their ambassadors for consultations after a German court ruled Iran ordered the 1992 murders of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
Smith said that an Iranian news agency report on Saturday of a trade ban against New Zealand had not been confirmed.
"There has been no official confirmation from Iran... there could have been some misunderstanding of this," he told a news conference.
